title: Cartesian product
primary_statement: X x Y = { (x,y) : x in X, y in Y }

title: Binary relation
primary_statement: a subset of X x X

title: Function
primary_statement: a relation that is single-valued and total

title: Injection
primary_statement: f(x)=f(y) implies x=y

title: Surjection
primary_statement: every y has a preimage

title: Bijection
primary_statement: injective and surjective

title: Composition of functions
primary_statement: (g o f)(x) = g(f(x))

title: Inverse function
primary_statement: f o f^{-1} = id and f^{-1} o f = id

title: Equivalence relation
primary_statement: reflexive, symmetric, transitive

title: Partitions and equivalence relations
primary_statement: equivalence relations correspond bijectively to partitions

title: Quotient set
primary_statement: X/~ is the set of equivalence classes

title: Well-definedness on a quotient
primary_statement: [x] -> [h(x)] is a function iff x~x' implies h(x)~h(x')

title: Axiom of choice
primary_statement: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function

title: Axiom of countable choice
primary_statement: a countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function

title: Peano axioms
primary_statement: 0 in N; S injective; 0 not a successor; induction

title: The natural numbers
primary_statement: a system (N,0,S) satisfying the Peano axioms

title: Induction
primary_statement: X contains 0 and is S-closed implies X = N

title: Recursion theorem
primary_statement: unique f with f(0)=a and f(S n)=g(n,f n)

title: Strong induction
primary_statement: if P holds at n whenever it holds below n then P holds everywhere

title: Well-ordering of N
primary_statement: every nonempty subset of N has a least element

title: Addition on N
primary_statement: a+0=a ; a+S(b)=S(a+b)

title: Order on N
primary_statement: a <= b iff exists c, a + c = b

title: Semiring laws on N
primary_statement: + and * are associative and commutative, * distributes over +

title: Cancellation in N
primary_statement: a+c=b+c implies a=b ; a*c=b*c and c!=0 implies a=b

title: No zero divisors in N
primary_statement: a*b=0 implies a=0 or b=0

title: Trichotomy in N
primary_statement: exactly one of a<b, a=b, a>b

title: Order compatibility in N
primary_statement: a<=b implies a+c<=b+c and a*c<=b*c

title: Division with remainder in N
primary_statement: for b>0, unique q,r with a = bq + r and 0 <= r < b

title: Commutative monoid
primary_statement: associative commutative binary op with identity

title: Commutative semiring
primary_statement: two monoids + distributivity, no additive inverses required

title: Commutative ring
primary_statement: commutative semiring with additive inverses

title: Integral domain
primary_statement: commutative ring, 1!=0, no zero divisors

title: Field
primary_statement: commutative ring in which every nonzero element is a unit

title: Ordered ring
primary_statement: ring with a total order compatible with + and with * by positives

title: Ordered integral domain
primary_statement: integral domain that is an ordered ring

title: Ordered field
primary_statement: field with a total order compatible with + and *

title: The integers
primary_statement: Z = (N x N)/~ , (a,b) ~ (c,d) iff a+d = b+c

title: The integer relation is an equivalence
primary_statement: ~_Z is reflexive symmetric transitive

title: Z operations are well defined
primary_statement: + , * , - respect ~_Z

title: Order on Z
primary_statement: [(a,b)] <= [(c,d)] iff a+d <= b+c in N

title: Z is a commutative ring
primary_statement: (Z,+,*,0,1) satisfies the ring axioms

title: Z is an integral domain
primary_statement: Z has no zero divisors and 1 != 0

title: Z is an ordered integral domain
primary_statement: the order on Z is total and compatible with + and *

title: N embeds in Z
primary_statement: n -> [(n,0)] is an injective semiring and order homomorphism

title: Cancellation in Z
primary_statement: ac = bc and c != 0 imply a = b

title: Well-ordering of bounded-below sets in Z
primary_statement: a nonempty subset of Z bounded below has a least element

title: Division with remainder in Z
primary_statement: for b != 0, unique q,r with a = bq + r and 0 <= r < |b|

title: GCD and Bezout's identity
primary_statement: gcd(a,b) exists and equals ax + by for some integers x,y

title: The rationals
primary_statement: Q = (Z x Z*)/~ , (a,b) ~ (c,d) iff ad = bc

title: The rational relation is an equivalence
primary_statement: ~_Q is an equivalence relation (transitivity uses that Z is a domain)

title: Q operations are well defined
primary_statement: + , * , inverse respect ~_Q

title: Order on Q
primary_statement: [(a,b)] with b>0 is <= [(c,d)] with d>0 iff ad <= bc in Z

title: Q is a field
primary_statement: every nonzero rational has a multiplicative inverse

title: Q is an ordered field
primary_statement: the order on Q is total and compatible with + and *

title: Z embeds in Q
primary_statement: a -> [(a,1)] is an injective ordered ring homomorphism

title: Q is the field of fractions of Z
primary_statement: Q is the smallest field containing Z, up to unique isomorphism

title: Lowest-terms representative
primary_statement: every rational equals a/b with gcd(a,b)=1 and b>0, uniquely

title: Q is Archimedean
primary_statement: for every x in Q there is n in N with n > x

title: The order on Q is dense
primary_statement: between any two rationals lies a third

title: Absolute value on Q
primary_statement: |x| = x if x>=0 else -x ; triangle inequality holds

title: The square root of 2 is irrational
primary_statement: no rational x satisfies x^2 = 2

title: Cauchy sequence of rationals
primary_statement: forall eps>0 in Q exists N forall m,n>=N |x_m - x_n| < eps

title: Q is not order-complete
primary_statement: { x in Q : x^2 < 2 } is nonempty and bounded above but has no supremum in Q

title: Q is not Cauchy-complete
primary_statement: there is a Cauchy sequence of rationals with no limit in Q

title: Dedekind cut
primary_statement: a nonempty proper downward-closed subset of Q with no greatest element

title: The real numbers
primary_statement: R is the set of Dedekind cuts of Q

title: Order on R
primary_statement: A <= B iff A is a subset of B ; this order is total

title: Addition on R
primary_statement: A + B = { a + b : a in A, b in B } ; again a cut

title: Negation on R
primary_statement: -A = { p in Q : -p is an upper bound of A but not the least one }

title: Multiplication on R
primary_statement: defined for positive cuts then extended by sign

title: R is an ordered field
primary_statement: (R,+,*,0*,1*,<=) satisfies the ordered-field axioms

title: Q embeds in R
primary_statement: q -> q* = { p in Q : p < q } is an injective ordered field homomorphism

title: The least-upper-bound property of R
primary_statement: every nonempty subset of R bounded above has a supremum, namely the union of its cuts

title: R is Archimedean
primary_statement: for every x in R there is n in N with n > x

title: Q is dense in R
primary_statement: between any two reals lies a rational

title: Existence of nth roots
primary_statement: for x > 0 in R and n in N+ there is a unique y > 0 with y^n = x

title: Absolute value on R
primary_statement: |x| = max(x, -x) ; triangle inequality holds

title: R as the Cauchy completion of Q
primary_statement: R' = (Cauchy sequences of rationals)/(null sequences)

title: The two constructions of R agree
primary_statement: the Dedekind and Cauchy constructions are isomorphic ordered fields

title: Uniqueness of the real number system
primary_statement: any two Dedekind-complete ordered fields are uniquely order-isomorphic

title: Finite set
primary_statement: in bijection with { k in N : k < n } for some n

title: Countable set
primary_statement: admits an injection into N

title: N x N is countable
primary_statement: pi(m,n) = (m+n)(m+n+1)/2 + n is a bijection N x N -> N

title: Countable union of countable sets
primary_statement: a countable union of countable sets is countable (uses countable choice)

title: Z is countable
primary_statement: Z is a countable union of finite sets

title: Q is countable
primary_statement: Q injects into Z x Z* which is countable

title: Cantor's theorem
primary_statement: there is no surjection from X onto its power set

title: The diagonal argument
primary_statement: from any sequence of reals in [0,1] one can construct a real it omits

title: Schroeder-Bernstein theorem
primary_statement: injections X -> Y and Y -> X give a bijection X -> Y

title: R is uncountable
primary_statement: there is no surjection from N onto R
